itineraries.title: Teardrop of Joy - 5 Day Itinerary
editorial: Colombo is the obvious way in or out for most international travellers, so our loop began and ended in the capital. In five days we went from the hilltop of Sigiriya to the hill station of Ella, and eventually the beaches of Mirissa.
What if we had more time?
We’d take the long route from Dambulla to Ella, with pitstops in Kandy for the Temple of the Tooth and Nuwara Eliya for the tea country.
With another couple of days, we’d also be tempted to slow down rather than add destinations. Sri Lanka rewards lingering more than rushing.

days.title: Day 1 - Sigiriya
editorial: We landed early in Colombo and took a pre-booked taxi towards Sigiriya, stopping at Dambulla along the way.

The Dambulla cave temple was one of the calmest places on the trip. The artwork covering the cave ceilings is far more intricate than the outside prepares you for, while the reclining Buddha statues appear almost to emerge from the rock itself.
We reached Sigiriya, took a nap and started the climb around 4:00 PM. It took us roughly an hour to get to the top, although you could easily spend longer stopping for views.
You can hire guides at both Dambulla and Sigiriya, but we chose introspection over information. Nobody pestered us about it, which improved the experience considerably.
Sigiriya is a little like Machu Picchu lite—less dramatic, far easier to reach and roughly a millennium older. The site was also exceptionally clean despite receiving visitors from everywhere.

days.title: Day 2 - Ella
editorial: Leave early for Ella.

Our four-hour taxi ride was almost as memorable as the destination because the driver simply… drove. No incessant honking, no phone calls every five minutes, no attempt to turn a mountain road into a qualifying lap.

Ella is bougie in the nicest possible way: misty hills and tea country wrapped around cafés, guesthouses and lots of foreign travellers. It reminded us of Munnar if Munnar had borrowed some of Langkawi’s tourist infrastructure.

Walk along the train tracks to the Nine Arches Bridge, then continue towards Little Adam’s Peak for sunset. There is a shorter route from town, which we discovered only after choosing the scenic-but-longer version.

days.title: Day 3 - Ella + Mirissa
editorial: We liked the Nine Arches walk enough to repeat it the next morning.

Even in mid-March, the hills were astonishingly lush. Sri Lanka often felt more rainforest-green than large parts of the Indian subcontinent, with a variety of trees and vegetation that made the drive south feel continuously scenic.
After checking out, drive down to Mirissa. The highway stretch towards the south coast was excellent and dramatically faster than the narrow hill roads.
We reached Mirissa around sunset, which is exactly when a beach town should introduce itself. The pace drops, the light softens and suddenly doing nothing feels like an itinerary item.

days.title: Day 4 - Mirissa
editorial: We slept in instead of going whale-watching or snorkelling. No regrets.
Most water activities leave early because the sea is calmer in the morning, so decide the night before whether you actually want to participate. We chose laziness.
For around 2,000 Sri Lankan rupees each when we visited, we got beach beds with coconut water and iced coffee included. That felt like an extremely rational exchange of money for happiness.

Spend the evening walking the beach. Mirissa and Ella both used warm, soft lighting particularly well; a small detail, but one that made their tourist areas feel much calmer than places lit like cricket stadiums.

days.title: Day 5 - Colombo
editorial: Drive back to Colombo and leave enough buffer before your flight.
One of us had spent time here as a child, so we walked around Galle Face partly to reminisce. Colombo remains, in our view, the most orderly major city in South Asia.
We also stopped at Seema Malakaya, where Buddha statues overlook the lake in the middle of the city. Despite the traffic outside, the temple feels remarkably serene.

If you have time, One Galle Face is a polished modern mall nearby. It is exactly what you expect from a polished modern mall, which can be either praise or criticism depending on how long you have been travelling.
